requirements.evidence: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:56 matches the contract signature; :61-66 treat null/empty/whitespace as a no-op before any HTTP call; :68-71 POST JSON {content} with timeout(5)/connectTimeout(3); :84-92 build title/message/key=value lines and truncate with mb_substr to 1800; :49 SENSITIVE_KEY covers password|token|secret|authorization|api[_-]?key|webhook case-insensitively; :101-108 recurse into nested arrays; :110 redacts Bearer strings; :127 renders arrays as JSON; :73-78 log non-2xx and transport errors at error level, with :149-161 scrubbing the URL. config/logging.php:172 defaults the stack to daily; :181 daily days 14; :185-191 add the audit channel (daily, audit.log, level info, 90 days); no discord channel. config/services.php:201-203, .env.example:10-18 and phpunit.xml:282 are all present. docs/ops/observability.md is added.

conventions.evidence: Sibling config style is matched and PHPDoc is on the public method (DiscordOpsAlert.php:37-56), as the task asked. The Pest test ships with the change. Deviations: conventions.md points to `docs/ops/logging.md` for logging guidance, but the change adds `docs/ops/observability.md`, so that reference stays dangling. No CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] entry is in the diff.

security.evidence: Key-based and Bearer redaction is applied recursively (DiscordOpsAlert.php:95-119). The webhook URL is scrubbed from exception messages, including encoded forms, the path and a generic /webhooks/ regex fallback (:149-161). The non-2xx log carries only the status (:74). Every failure is caught, including logging failures (:76-78, :136-143). No user-facing input surface.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php covers: the no-op for '' and null (:302-309); formatting, key/Bearer/nested redaction and the readable value (:311-329); multibyte truncation to exactly 1800 (:331-336); non-2xx and transport-error logging without the token (:338-354); and the logging config (:356-363). Gaps: no assertion on the daily/audit path values, no check of Bearer inside a nested array, and the global `const WEBHOOK` (:300) can collide with other test files.

simplicity.evidence: A single small class built on the HTTP client and Log facade. Some defensive extras go slightly beyond what is needed: Stringable branches (:114-116, :128), scrubbing of rawurlencode/urlencode variants plus the path plus a regex fallback (:152-160), and a nested try in logFailure (:136-143).

readability.evidence: Named constants (:45-51) and small private methods (buildText, redact, format, logFailure, scrub) with clear names and a class docblock explaining intent. No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file in the diff serves the task (.env.example, notifier, logging/services config, docs/ops, phpunit.xml, test). Nothing is wired into jobs or handlers, which matches the out-of-scope list.

issues.explanation: conventions.md links logging guidance to docs/ops/logging.md, but the lanes doc was added as observability.md, so the project's reference points to a file this change does not create.
The docs-sync convention requires an entry under [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md; the diff has none.
A global `const WEBHOOK` in a Pest file lives in the global namespace and will cause a redefinition error if another test file declares the same constant.
The logging-config test does not assert the daily/audit file paths or audit.driver against the contract's path requirements, and does not cover Bearer redaction inside nested arrays.
Scrubbing tries several encodings, the path and a regex fallback; this is defensible for secrecy but more than the minimum needed.

review.summary: The change adds a soft-failing, redacting DiscordOpsAlert notifier, the daily/audit logging lanes, env keys, the phpunit pin and a lanes decision guide, and it meets every requirement and contract item. Tests cover the main behaviours and the failure paths. Remaining gaps are minor convention ones (the doc filename does not match the conventions' docs/ops/logging.md reference, and there is no CHANGELOG entry), plus small test nits, so I would approve with nits.
